findings.note: HB 278, Protect Military Votes. Ager is listed among the primary sponsors in the filed version (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H278v1.pdf). The bill would write into law that a covered military or overseas voter returning an absentee ballot does not have to include a photocopy of photo ID or a sworn ID-exception statement. Referred to committee; no further action shown.
subjects: photo ID with military and overseas absentee ballots

findings.note: HB 1246, Safeguarding Elections Act. Ager is listed as a co-sponsor. One part of the bill (G.S. 163-274(a)(17)) would make it a misdemeanor to demand citizenship documentation from a voter beyond what state law requires, at any point in the voting process. Another part keeps photocopies of voter ID confidential. Referred to committee; no further action shown.

provenance.fetched_by: source-collector

findings.note: HB 1230, No Federal Interference in Elections. Ager is listed as a co-sponsor. The bill adds photocopies of identification for voting and voter photo-ID photographs to the confidential voter data that election boards may not hand to federal agencies without a court order or judge-signed warrant. Referred to committee; no further action shown.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (final House passage vote, 66 aye, 47 no)
findings.note: Ager is recorded No. The bill text (ratified version: https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) removes deceased voters from the rolls weekly, requires the State Board to set up a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database, and requires a registration application to affirmatively state US citizenship, with a sworn statement if the answer is left blank. The vote record does not say why he voted no.
